fields.description:
## Symptom

Five tests in `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` fail locally for any
developer whose git config sets `safe.bareRepository = explicit`. They pass under git's default
(`all`), which is what CI uses, so **CI can never exercise this path**.

Failing: `test_relevant_remote_rejection_never_places_candidate_on_shared_head`,
`test_successful_push_followed_by_remote_rewrite_fails_closed`,
`test_unrelated_remote_rejection_merges_and_rebuilds_private_candidate`,
`test_lost_push_ack_is_confirmed_without_publishing_a_second_bundle`,
`test_post_push_convergence_preserves_concurrent_local_delivery_pending`.

All five fail identically — not an assertion, a `CalledProcessError` from the test helper:

```
subprocess.CalledProcessError: Command '['git', '-C',
 '.../tickets-remote.git', 'ls-tree', '-r', '--name-only',
 'refs/heads/tickets', '5c21-6a58-bfa5-4202']' returned non-zero exit status 128
```

## Root cause

`git` refuses to **discover** a bare repository via `-C` / cwd when `safe.bareRepository=explicit`;
it accepts one named by a top-level `--git-dir`. Exit 128 is a refusal to open the repository at
all, *before* any ref lookup:

```
git -C <bare>  -> fatal: cannot use bare repository '<bare>' (safe.bareRepository is 'explicit')
git --git-dir <bare>  -> exit 0
```

The offending helper is `_git` at `tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py:40-46`,
which hardcodes `["git", "-C", str(repo), *args]`. The bare remote is built in `_ticket_remote`
(:97-117) and read at **:401, :402, :415, :423, :435, :455, :493, :576** — eight sites across the
five failing tests.

Two claims in the original report are wrong and must not be carried forward: (1) the
`refs/heads/tickets` ref EXISTS and resolves fine — git never gets as far as looking it up; (2)
git 2.55.0 is a red herring — `safe.bareRepository` shipped in git 2.38.0 (2022-10-03) with exactly
these semantics, so there is no version regression to chase.

## This is a recurrence of a class already fixed

Closed ticket `3476-4472-3407-4246` (`embolismic-adverse-dragon`) records the governing policy
verbatim: "the supported test suite must run both locally and in CI. **Treat agents dismissing
reproducible local test failures as environmental noise as an anti-pattern.**" That ticket
converted 13 files from `git -C <bare>` to `git --git-dir <bare>` and added the held-out oracle
`tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py`.

**Why this file escaped the guard:** that oracle pins a **hardcoded allowlist** of fixture nodes
(`_FIXTURE_NODES`, 3 entries). `test_atomic_completion_close.py` was added on 2026-08-25 by commit
`1cb1cdd25aff` — four days *after* the guard landed — and reintroduced the banned construct. There
is no static sweep either (`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py` covers an unrelated concern). The
guard only checks three files that were already fixed, so it cannot fail when a new file
reintroduces the defect. **That allowlist is why this is the second occurrence, and leaving it is
why there would be a third.**

## Plan

1. **Point fix.** Add a sibling helper `_git_bare(remote, *args)` that addresses the bare remote
   with a top-level `--git-dir`, and route only the bare-remote call sites through it. `_git` is
   also used on **non-bare** worktrees (`tracker`, `writer`, `tmp_path` for `init`/`clone`), so a
   blanket `-C` -> `--git-dir` swap is wrong.
2. **Close the oracle gap.** Replace the hand-maintained `_FIXTURE_NODES` allowlist in
   `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py` with a **tree-derived**
   static AST scan over every file under `tests/`. Per module, derive the identifiers bound to a
   bare repository from every `--bare` idiom actually present in this tree:
   - the last path operand after the flag — `git init --bare <dir>`, and `git clone --bare <src>
     <dst>`, whose *source* must not be marked;
   - the directory the call runs in when the flag takes no operand — `_git(remote, "init", "-q",
     "--bare")`, the shape the already-fixed integration fixtures use;
   - a name bound by a bare-repository factory — `init_bare_remote(remote)` (a `bare`-named
     creator taking only paths), or a same-module helper that creates a bare repository **and
     returns it**. Return positions are tracked, so `return remote, writer` marks only the first
     element and a helper returning the *worktree* marks nothing; and the mark is applied to the
     **caller's binding name**, read off the assignment, so a rename
     (`origin, scribe = _ticket_remote(...)`) is still covered.
   Marking is otherwise **module-scoped by identifier**, which covers the same flow a second way
   when the caller reuses the helper's own name. Then flag any `-C` invocation targeting a marked
   name — direct, or through a module-local helper that forwards its first parameter to `-C`. Two
   calls are **exempt**: one carrying the inline `-c safe.bareRepository=all` opt-in, which is the
   deliberate escape ticket 3476 preserved in `tests/scripts/test_reconcile_bridge_push_retry.py`
   and which passes under the strict config today; and the **creating** call, since
   `git -C <dir> init --bare` runs before `<dir>` is a repository and so has nothing to discover.
   Pin the underlying git behaviour the rule encodes, and self-test the detector on synthetic
   modules (offending, renamed-binding, and escaped), so neither can rot silently.
   The guard stays a **pytest oracle** rather than a `scripts/check_*.py` wired into `make lint`:
   it replaces the held-out oracle that failed, and a new gate script would be a new `ci_gate`
   mechanism that `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` fails on.
3. Fix every file the tree-derived scan flags, so the guard is green on landing. It flags 12 sites
   in 2 files: 8 in the file under fix and 4 in `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py`,
   whose `test_fresh_clone_json_exposes_allocation_without_a_policy_verdict` and
   `test_invalid_configured_branch_cleans_only_its_temporary_child` fail under the strict config
   today for exactly the same reason.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=<file setting safe.bareRepository=explicit> GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py` exits 0 with 17 passed (today: 5 failed, 12 passed).
- [ ] The same file still passes under default git config (17 passed), and the full `pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle` run still passes.
- [ ] `tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py` passes under the strict config too (today: 2 failed, 5 passed), and under the default config.
- [ ] A regression oracle in `tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py` fails deterministically if the `git -C <bare-repo>` construct is reintroduced anywhere under `tests/`; demonstrated by temporarily reverting one call site, observing the guard go RED, and restoring it.
- [ ] The guard's coverage is derived from the tree, not from a hand-maintained file allowlist: `_FIXTURE_NODES` is gone, and adding a new bare-fixture test that uses `git -C <bare>` fails without any registration step.

## Testing

- Reproduce RED first: `env GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=$STRICT GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py -q` must show `5 failed, 12 passed` before the fix and `17 passed` after.
- Default-config run of the same file: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_atomic_completion_close.py -q` -> 17 passed.
- Directory regression: `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle -q`, plus `python -m pytest tests/interfaces/test_tracker_footprint_cli.py -q` under both configs.
- Guard: `python -m pytest tests/integration/test_bare_repository_fixture_portability_heldout.py -q`, plus a mutation run with one call site reverted to `_git(remote, ...)` to prove the guard goes RED.
- Ratchets and gates: `make lint` (module-size, `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`, `check_mechanism_delta.py --check`) and `make typecheck`.
